title: Foot-Strike Pattern and Performance in a Marathon
publisher: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
claims: Foot-strike classification, gender and race rank were recorded at the 8.1 km mark for 2112 runners in the 2011 Milwaukee Lakefront Marathon.
Of 1991 runners classified, heel-strike prevalence was 93.67% (n = 1865).
A significant difference between foot-strike classification and performance was found (Kruskal-Wallis, p < .0001), with more elite performers less likely to heel strike.
No significant difference between foot-strike classification and gender was found.
The study is cross-sectional and observational; it does not show that changing foot strike changes performance.
license: Publisher terms; citation and summary only

claimVerification.note: 原文：“Foot-strike classification … gender, and rank (position in race) were recorded at the 8.1-km mark for 2112 runners at the 2011 Milwaukee Lakefront Marathon.”
原文：“1991 runners were classified by foot-strike pattern, revealing a heel-strike prevalence of 93.67% (n = 1865).”
原文：名次与着地分类差异显著（Kruskal-Wallis χ2=32.85, df=3, P<.0001），“with more elite performers being less likely to heel strike”；属横断面名次关联，非干预结果。

原文：“A Fisher exact test between foot-strike classification and gender for all 1991 runners revealed a nonsignificant trend … (P = .0727)”，摘要亦写“No significant difference”。claim 的“无显著差异”成立，但原文有非显著趋势（男性更少后跟着地）。
原文：“This study was an observational cohort study”，着地分类仅在 8.1 km 处单次观测、成绩取完赛名次；因此“不能证明改变着地方式会改变成绩”是由设计推出的方法学判断，原文未直接讨论因果，但与该设计一致。
